intent.quote: I fear that there are actually many duplicates, or that the actual definition of an SR is actually blur currently in the plumb project.
intent.readback: The records are your intent written down, and there are few of them: each requirement states one durable behaviour you can observe, with examples and a proof. Every record is hashed so a change of meaning shows and its links go stale, and nothing is lost: a record is only retired, with a trail to what replaced it. A fix of a behaviour already stated goes under that requirement, never a new one, and each principle you state is one intent.
will: Keep every record as a Markdown file named by its frontmatter id, with a hash that changes only when its meaning changes.
Pin both ends of every link, report a moved end as stale, and change links only through logged repin, unlink and relink.
Keep an append-only, hash-chained log, one never-edited file per entry, with tampering reported.
Hold one durable observable behaviour per requirement; claim a fix under the requirement it restores.
Retire a replaced record with a supersedes trail; it stops reaching you and stops being checked, and its uncarried examples' tests are unlinked.
Capture your words as a pre-intent with context and write the formal records in one call, naming the requirements the new intent changes.
Import pi-agent-factory's records read-only and idempotently, approving only what an upstream human consent pins.
wont: Delete a record without a supersedes trail.
Create a new requirement for a fix of a behaviour already stated.
Ask you to read records, cards or ids to approve them: a judge-validated interpretation counts (P3, P9).
Edit or remove a log entry outside the archive compaction of P15.
Write to the pi-agent-factory source during an import.
assumptions: Repin, unlink and relink are the agent's commands; they take record ids, which P2 allows since no owner command does.
'Approved' covers both the owner's answer and a judge-validated interpretation (P3); the only-test refusal protects both.
The P15 compaction of old log entries into archive segments is the only sanctioned rewrite of the log, and validate still chains through it; that behaviour is P15's requirement, not this one's.
The legacy events.jsonl and evidence.jsonl migration (SR-074) has run, so reading the legacy format is not a durable behaviour.

SR-059's clause that a by-import approval is written only after the owner confirms it in their own terminal goes: under P2 the owner runs no command, so the import writes it from a matching consent and an agent-appended one never counts.
Anchors SR-149, SR-195 and SR-165 carry no feature; the link and retirement requirements go under FEAT-001 (records core, as SR-003 and SR-001), capture under FEAT-002 (as SR-034 and SR-035).

requirements.title: A record is a Markdown file named by its id, hashed by its meaning
requirements.statement: plumb keeps every record (INT, SR, DEC, FEAT, NC) as a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter under .plumb/; its identity is its frontmatter id, never its filename; a malformed or duplicate id is reported. Its content hash covers the meaning (every frontmatter field except links, plus the normalized body), so it ignores YAML style, key order, CRLF and trailing whitespace and changes when the meaning changes.

examples.given: a file .plumb/requirements/anything.md whose frontmatter id is SR-007
examples.then: the record is SR-007, whatever the filename

examples.given: two record files that carry the same id SR-001
examples.then: it reports a duplicate-id error naming both files

examples.given: a record whose frontmatter id is SR-1x
examples.then: it is rejected as a malformed id

examples.given: a record with a pinned hash
examples.when: the file is re-saved with CRLF line endings, reordered keys and trailing spaces
examples.then: its hash is unchanged

examples.given: a record with a pinned hash
examples.then: its hash changes and every link pinned to it goes stale

examples.given: a linked source file
examples.when: it is re-saved with CRLF line endings and no other change
examples.then: the file end's hash is unchanged

examples.given: a record whose only change is a new link in its links list
examples.then: the hash is unchanged, since links are not part of the meaning

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: the AI shows, in a scratch repository, a record renamed on disk still loading under its id, a CRLF re-save leaving its hash and links current, and a one-word change of its statement turning its links stale in the status.

requirements.title: A link pins both ends and changes only through logged commands
requirements.statement: A link lives in its source record and pins the content hash of both ends; plumb reports it stale (naming which end moved) when either hash differs, dangling (an error) when its target is missing, unpinned (a warning) without a pin. Links are repinned, removed or moved only through the agent's repin, unlink and relink commands, each logging the old and new ends, unlink and relink with a required note; none of them approves a record.

examples.then: it exits 1 saying there is no such link, and the record file is unchanged

examples.when: unlink or relink runs without a note
examples.then: it exits with a usage error and changes nothing

examples.then: it is refused, saying the approved example would lose its only test and naming relink instead; the record is unchanged

requirements.title: The log is append-only, one hash-chained file per entry
requirements.statement: Every log entry is written through one append function as its own JSON file under .plumb/log/<kind>/, created without replacing and never edited, carrying its digest and the previous entry's digest found from a rebuildable head pointer; branches that both append never conflict and a forked chain is accepted. plumb validate reports an edited entry, a removed entry a later one names, and an unparsable file. An entry is visible to the next reader as soon as it is appended, within one worker pass too.

examples.given: two worktrees that each append approvals, prompts and test runs
examples.when: one branch is merged into the other
examples.then: git reports no conflict under .plumb/log and plumb validate accepts the forked chain

examples.given: two writers in one worktree in the same second
examples.then: two distinct files exist and neither replaced the other

examples.given: a committed entry file edited by hand
examples.then: it reports that file as modified

examples.given: the head pointer in .plumb/cache was deleted
examples.then: its prev is the stream's latest entry, found by a scan

examples.given: an entry file deleted while a later entry names it as prev
examples.then: it reports the missing entry

examples.given: a file under .plumb/log that is not valid JSON
examples.then: it reports the file as unparsable

examples.given: a batch of verdicts interrupted after some entries were written
examples.then: it extends the chain from the last entry actually on disk, not from an older head pointer

examples.given: a worker pass running several jobs
examples.when: an earlier job appends its verdicts
examples.then: a later job in the same pass reads those entries, and the pass's final progress counts every job

examples_dropped.why: same rule as SR-073/EX-3 (an edited entry is reported), now said of an entry file rather than a line
same rule as SR-073/EX-1 (branches merge without a log conflict, the forked chain is accepted)
interleaved lines cannot happen with one file per entry; SR-073/EX-2 states the rule that holds

bounded batches that cut head and lock operations are a performance tactic of the worker, not a behaviour the owner can observe; what holds (each verdict its own chained entry) is this requirement's statement
coalescing identical progress writes is a performance tactic; what the owner sees of progress is P12's and P13's progress requirements

requirements.title: A replaced record is retired with its trail, and its tests follow
requirements.statement: A superseded record is retired, not deleted: its history and supersedes trail stay, it no longer reaches the owner or the staleness check, tests of the examples the new record carries relink to it, others are unlinked, and plumb validate warns about a retired example still verified by a test. plumb reports a deleted record only through the links that named it.

examples.given: an old requirement describes behaviour a newer one replaced
examples.when: the newer one is linked as superseding it
examples.then: the old one's links no longer appear among the stale links and no question reaches the owner about them

examples.given: a requirement that still describes current behaviour but whose links moved
examples.then: it is repinned, not retired

examples.given: SR-002 supersedes SR-001 and SR-001/EX-1, which SR-002 does not carry, is still verified by tests/test_a.py
examples.then: it warns [retired-example] that SR-001/EX-1 is retired by SR-002 but still verified by tests/test_a.py and says to unlink the test and drop it when it covers nothing else; it never says to move the test to SR-002 or keep SR-001

examples.given: SR-001 is approved, SR-002 supersedes it, and SR-001#3 is the only test of SR-001/EX-2
examples.when: the agent unlinks SR-001#3 with a note
examples.then: the link is removed: a superseded record's example is retired, so the only-test refusal does not protect it

examples.given: a test function whose sr markers name only superseded records and that no live record links to
examples.then: the test function is deleted (the whole file when nothing live remains); a test a live record still links to stays and only loses the retired id from its marker

examples.given: SR-001 has two tests verifying EX-1 and SR-002 supersedes it verifying neither
examples.then: both links are warned, one per link

examples.given: a commit with trailer SR-001 that unlinks tests/test_a.py from SR-001 and deletes the file
examples.when: plumb claims check runs over it
examples.then: tests/test_a.py is declared: a path a claimed record linked in the commit's parent counts

examples.given: a record file deleted outright instead of superseded
examples.then: the links naming it are reported dangling; a deleted record no link names is not reported, so the never-delete rule is the agent's skill's

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: in a scratch repository, the AI supersedes a requirement and shows the status listing no stale link from the retired one, plumb explain on it reaching its successor, and validate warning about a test left on a retired example until it is unlinked.

requirements.title: A requirement is one durable behaviour, and a fix goes under its requirement
requirements.statement: Each requirement states one durable observable behaviour with examples and a proof, under a feature; a fix of a stated behaviour is claimed under its requirement (or an NC when it was broken), never as a new requirement; one intent per principle; a newer decision wins over an older example's test. No plumb check enforces this: the rule lives in plumb's plumb-records skill, which the agent follows, and in commit trailers that claim the requirement fixed.

examples.given: plumb's installed plumb-records skill
examples.then: it says each requirement states one durable observable behaviour, a fix of a stated behaviour is claimed under its requirement or recorded as an NC, never as a new requirement, there is one intent per principle, and a record is retired through a superseding record, never deleted

examples.given: a behaviour a requirement states is broken (a background process opens a console window)
examples.then: the fixing commit's trailer claims that requirement, and no new requirement appears

examples.given: a newer decision changed a behaviour that an older approved example's test still asserts
examples.then: the agent's plumb-records skill tells it that the test follows the newer decision and the older example is reworded or superseded through the judge cascade, and that the owner is not asked per test

examples_dropped.why: it describes the version 2 landing itself, a one-time event rather than a durable behaviour; the retirement it relies on is carried by the retirement requirement

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: the AI fixes a broken behaviour in a scratch repository and shows the commit's trailer naming its requirement with no new requirement written, and the skill's text stating the rule.

requirements.title: Capture turns the owner's words into linked records in one call
requirements.statement: One capture call keeps the owner's words with their context as a pre-intent and writes the agent's formal intent, requirement and decision records with pinned links, ids allocated without collision, all proposed until the judge cascade validates them; the quote must be verbatim in the logged prompt.

examples.given: a capture document with the owner's quote and context, a formal intent, one requirement with two examples and one decision
examples.then: one pre-intent, one INT, one SR with EX-1 and EX-2 and one DEC exist, each proposed, the SR and DEC derived from the INT and the INT from the pre-intent, and the output is text for the agent, not a card for the owner

examples.given: a capture document whose quote is not a verbatim span of the logged prompt
examples.then: it exits 2 and writes nothing

examples.given: a document updating the examples of an approved SR
examples.then: the SR becomes an unconfirmed edit and goes back through the judge cascade; no question reaches the owner while the judge finds the change keeps the older intent

examples.given: any capture document
examples.then: it prints what it would write and writes no file and no event

examples.given: SR-004 has EX-1 and EX-2
examples.when: the agent adds an example to SR-004
examples.then: SR-004 gains EX-3; an approved SR-004 becomes an unconfirmed edit, a proposed one stays proposed

examples.given: the judge cascade validates a captured interpretation
examples.then: they are marked judge-approved and the trail from the pre-intent to each formal record is kept

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: in a live session the owner states a small new intent in plain words; the AI then shows the pre-intent with its context, the formal records derived from it, and the judge's verdict marking them approved, all without the owner reading a card.

requirements.title: A decision keeps its alternatives and changes only by a superseding decision
requirements.statement: A decision records the question, the chosen option, its alternatives and whether it matters; it is never edited to change its choice: a new decision supersedes it and the old one stays unchanged.

examples.given: two readings of a request fit
examples.when: the agent records a decision choosing A with B as alternative and matters true
examples.then: a DEC with chosen A, alternatives [B] and matters true is written, proposed

examples.given: DEC-020 is approved
examples.when: the agent records a decision superseding DEC-020 with B chosen
examples.then: a new DEC with a supersedes link to DEC-020 is written and DEC-020 is unchanged

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: the AI records a decision with an alternative in a scratch repository, then supersedes it, and shows both records with the old one unchanged.

requirements.title: A capture names the requirements its new intent changes or contradicts
requirements.statement: When an intent is captured, plumb finds the existing requirements whose meaning it changes or contradicts and names them by title in the capture output for the agent, so the same capture supersedes or rewords them instead of leaving them to go stale; a contradiction it cannot resolve reaches the owner only as one question to arbitrate.

examples.given: a new intent removes behaviour that existing requirements still describe
examples.then: the capture output for the agent names those requirements by title, and the same capture supersedes or rewords each, so none is left describing the removed behaviour

examples.given: a new requirement says the agent relays the owner's conflict choice while another says it never does
examples.then: the capture output for the agent names the contradiction, nothing is approved, and it reaches the owner only as one question-tool question to arbitrate

examples.given: the owner states a new principle
examples.then: one intent records it, and the capture output for the agent names the requirements it changes

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: in a live session the owner states an intent that removes a behaviour an existing requirement describes; the agent's capture output names that requirement and the same capture supersedes it.

requirements.title: The pi-agent-factory import is read-only, idempotent and never manufactures approval
requirements.statement: plumb import reads pi-agent-factory's register (requirements, features with bundles, NCs and their relations as symbol and test-node link ends) without writing to it; a dry run prints the plan; a repeated import changes nothing. Every imported record is proposed, except a requirement whose upstream human consent pins its current content, which is approved by import citing that consent; an approval the agent appended itself never approves.

examples.then: it prints create lines for every record and the target is unchanged

examples.given: a target after one import
examples.then: no file changes and no import event is appended

examples.given: the source SR-003 statement changed
examples.then: the plan shows update SR-003 statement and the record is rewritten, re-pinned and proposed

examples.then: SR-078 is proposed

examples.then: it is ignored and the SR is proposed

examples.given: a by import approval the agent appended itself, not written by an import from a matching consent
examples.then: SR-077 stays proposed and the approval is ignored

examples.when: it is imported into a target holding src/x.py
examples.then: the link names src/x.py::fn and an edit elsewhere in src/x.py leaves it current

examples.given: FEAT-001 lists SR-050 that its bundle lacks
examples.then: FEAT-001's requirements include SR-050 and a membership-difference finding names it

examples.given: any import
examples.then: the source tree's files and git status are unchanged

examples.given: a pi-agent-factory checkout with an approved SR-012 and no consent file
examples.then: SR-012 is imported as proposed and the checkout is unchanged

proof.plan: Recommended for the owner to decide: the AI imports the pi-agent-factory fixture twice into a scratch target and shows the dry-run plan, the second run changing nothing, the source's git status unchanged, and only the consent-pinned requirement approved by import.

decisions.question: When a link is removed, what happens to the numbers of the links after it?
decisions.chosen: they move down by one, and the command prints every new number
alternatives: leave a removed placeholder so numbers never change

decisions.question: Who may remove or move a link?
decisions.chosen: the agent, like plumb link, with a required note logged; removing an approved example's only live test is refused
alternatives: only the owner from their own terminal

decisions.question: What is a requirement, and how is a record set replaced?
decisions.chosen: one durable observable behaviour with examples and a proof; a fix of a stated behaviour goes under its requirement; an intent is one per principle; a set is replaced in place, older records retired with a supersedes trail and one repin pass
alternatives: both shapes, each marked behaviour or change
purge the proposed records only and keep the confirmed ones as they are

decisions.question: What does a passing test on a retired example mean?
decisions.chosen: retired means gone: the test is unlinked, and deleted when it covers nothing live; the superseding record keeps only the tests of what it states
alternatives: the behaviour lives on: the test's marker, or the example itself, moves to the superseding record

decisions.question: When a newer decision changed a behaviour that an older approved example's test still asserts, do the tests follow the newer decision?
decisions.chosen: yes, the newer decision wins: the tests are updated to the newer behaviour and the older example is reworded or superseded, logged once
alternatives: settle each in the version 2 rewrite

retired_decisions.why: overturned by its own alternative: the log is one file per entry under .plumb/log/<kind>/ (INT-022, the append-only log requirement), not two JSONL streams
superseded by the full importer: a requirement whose upstream human consent pins its current content is approved by import (the import requirement); everything else stays proposed
matters false and an implementation choice; its rule (links live in their source record) is stated by the link requirement
